12164518810.name: Amis du Teche
12164518810.bio: Amis du Teche is steeped in the Louisiana Cajun music culture. Their rich connection with their hometown of Breaux Bridge and growing up along the banks of Bayou Teche have brought each member together. The bayou is where they met, jammed, performed, and now recorded.  With a very rich repertoire reaching deep into the archives of Cajun music classics, drawing from the best compositions of their contemporary peers, and now writing original songs to add to the rich archives of Cajun Music... the talent, cultural influences, and musical curiosity of Amis du Teche should peak the best of music lovers' and aficionados' curiosity as we watch this young vibrant band emerge!

12164564042.name: Mike Dopsie & Zydeco Entourage
12164564042.bio:
Mike Dopsie was born into dynamic royal family of Zydeco music. Born and raised in Lafayette,LA. He’s a third generation Zydeco Artist and fourth generation accordionist. He’s the Grandson of the late great Prince of Zydeco “Rockin’ Dopsie Sr.” The son of Grammy nominated, Louisiana Music Hall of Famer “Anthony Dopsie” and the nephew of grammy award winning Dwayne Dopsie, Rockin’ Dopsie Jr, and Tiger Dopsie.


Mike Dopsie’s style of zydeco consist of blues, r&b, and dabbles of jazz music.
Raised into the genre of zydeco music, but officially branched off and created into 
Mike Dopsie & Zydeco Entourage

12164581376.name: Karma and the Killjoys
12164581376.bio:
Karma and the Killjoys is classical piano turned rock band. Loud key-smashing chords dueling with gritty electric guitar, powerful, raw female voices and a thick chorus of harmonies is the strange and compelling concoction the band calls piano-rock. Ever pushing the bounds of what that means, Karma and the Killjoys expand their musicality with every song, both embracing and defying the genre–and therefore defining it. 

“Karma and the Killjoys have a palpable magic to them.” 
Jan Risher, The Advocate

Karma and the Killjoys is Rain Scott-Catoire (piano, vocals, songwriting), Sydni Myers (vocals, songwriting), Thomas Vercher (drums), and Tim Marchand (guitar).

12164553264.name: Brewmasters' Talk: Urban South Brewery
12164553264.bio:
The seed for Urban South was planted during the year I spent in Europe. Tasting Belgian and English ales and German lagers right from the source, I understood for the first time how big the chasm was between the beer my ancestors drank and the mass-market stuff I grew up with at home in South Louisiana. Naturally, as a good Cajun and Southerner, I knew I had to share the gospel of good beer.

At Urban South, we’re combining the heritage of European beer-making with the brashness of new American styles. With deep roots in Louisiana, our award-winning brewery inspires community with excellent craft beers that are easy to drink and perfect for the Southern climate. We operate with fearlessness and integrity in an effort to brew the South’s most respected beer.

Our vision is to build an enduring company that embodies the values and traditions of the Urban South. We seek to be strong community partners and produce world-class beer.

12164564073.name: Sonny Landreth
12164564073.bio:
Acclaimed guitarist’s new album mixes genres and styles
across a landscape of lyricism and rootsy grooves.

A percussive burst of acoustic resonator guitar pushes the narrator on a journey “between the life I left and the edge of next” in the title cut of guitarist, songwriter and bandleader Sonny Landreth’s 14th album. As the singer feels the wind at his back, a rising bass line intersects Landreth’s vocalizing to stretch the fingerpicked tune into Far Eastern melodicism.

12164503074.name: Rhiannon Giddens
12164503074.bio:
Rhiannon Giddens has made a singular, iconic career out of stretching her brand of folk music, with its miles-deep historical roots and contemporary sensibilities, into just about every field imaginable. A two-time GRAMMY Award and Pulitzer Prize-winning singer and instrumentalist, MacArthur “Genius” grant recipient, and composer of opera, ballet, and film, Giddens has centered her work around the mission of lifting up people whose contributions to American musical history have previously been overlooked or erased, and advocating for a more accurate understanding of the country’s musical origins through art.

As Pitchfork once said, “few artists are so fearless and so ravenous in their exploration”—a journey that has led to NPR naming her one of its 25 Most Influential Women Musicians of the 21st Century and to American Songwriter calling her “one of the most important musical minds currently walking the planet.”

12164581122.name: Country Gongbang
12164581122.bio:
Founded in 2014, Country Gongbang is South Korea’s first and only bluegrass band, pioneering a distinctive blend of contemporary bluegrass and K-pop sentiments. Singing in both English and Korean, they craft music that bridges cultural boundaries, carving a unique space in the global music scene.

In 2023, Country Gongbang received the prestigious International Band Performance Grant from the International Bluegrass Music Association (IBMA), recognizing their groundbreaking artistry. This honor led to their historic 2024 US tour, where they performed at renowned venues and festivals, including the legendary Grand Ole Opry in Nashville—marking the first-ever Korean band to grace its iconic stage. In September 2025, they were nominated for the 2025 IBMA Momentum Awards for Band of the Year and Vocalist of the Year, a historic recognition for a Korean bluegrass group on the international stage.

The group’s lineup features Yebin Kim on mandolin and lead vocals, Hyunho Jang on banjo, Jongsu Yoon on fiddle, Sunjae Won on guitar, and Keeha Song on bass.

Discover the vibrant fusion of tradition and innovation with Country Gongbang, where bluegrass transcends borders and embraces bold new horizons.

“South Korea’s Country Gongbang demonstrates that the basics of bluegrass aren’t limited exclusively to the realms of the western world.” — Bluegrass Today
“Their Korean-influenced repertoire epitomizes the talent, passion, and creativity growing in bluegrass music around the world!” — Paul Schiminger, IBMA’s former Executive Director

12164560859.name: Nomfusi
12164560859.bio:
In Nomfusi, the soul of Mama Afrika meets the fire of Motown and Soul… in a pint-sized packet of dynamite. Indeed, there is nothing small about the tiny songstress with the gigantic voice and tons of charm. With sheer will and determination, she has risen from the squalor of South African squatter camps to some of the major stages of the world. Likened by critics to a young Miriam Makeba with a twist of Tina Turner, the multiple SAMA and Metro FM Award nominee embraces both her African heritage and the sounds of Soul and Motown she grew up with. 
Nomfusi has given riveting performances across Europe and Canada at prestigious festivals such as WOMAD in England, performed with Angelique Kidjo at the Afrikadey Festival in Canada, and opened for superstar Lionel Richie at Stimmen Festival in Germany. She was chosen to portray the character of Miriam Makeba in “Long Walk To Freedom,” the film about the life of Nelson Mandela.
Nomfusi was raised by a single mother, a domestic worker by day, who was also a sangoma (African medicine woman) with a gift for music. She accompanied her mother to weekly rituals, where she developed her musicality by dancing and singing for hours. Tragically, she was orphaned at the age of 12 when her mother died of AIDS. With remarkable inner strength, Nomfusi turned her situation around to become one of South Africa’s brightest stars. She cares deeply for her community, while not shying away from the world of glitz, glamour and success. She does outreach work at schools for vulnerable children, speaks on symposia panels about the role of women and the arts in Africa, and works with South African NPO Mould, Empower, Serve, that helps homeless individuals get back on their feet. As she sings in her anthem against poverty, “Nontsokolo,”: “Remember your sister, your brother, your mother and your neighbor. Don’t leave them behind. Go back, and make a difference.”

12164527057.name: Brewmasters' Talk: Parish Brewing Co.
12164527057.bio:
Located in the heart of Cajun Country in Broussard, Louisiana, our simple goal is to make awesome craft brewed beer. Our story begins around 2003 when our founder Andrew moved from Louisiana to Pittsburgh and discovered a thriving craft beer scene. Returning home a few years later, he recognized a lack of breweries in Louisiana and set out to create part of what is now a thriving craft brewing industry.

Our first beer ever sold was Canebrake, named for the abounding sugarcane fields in the area, and it was a huge hit from the start. It didn’t help that Andrew was brewing in the "nano brewery," a tiny 50 gallon brewery, making just 20 kegs a week. Nevertheless, Parish was being distributed all over the Lafayette, La. region, and Canebrake was becoming more and more popular with a full range of beer drinkers—from light beer drinkers to 10th level beer nerds.We remain known in Louisiana for Canebrake, but the rest of the world knows us for Ghost in the Machine and our juice bomb IPAs and other innovations. In 2012, we completed construction on our new brewery on Jared Dr. and have been growing ever since. Today, we are one of the largest breweries in the region and distribute our beer throughout the south.

12164539221.name: Dustin Dale Gaspard
12164539221.bio:
Ambassador of his Cajun culture, bilingual Roots/ Blues Folk singer songwriter Dustin Dale Gaspard roars his legacy into existence. He sings "Je ne m’arreterai jamais" French words that are much more than just his lyrics- they are apart of his mission as a full time touring artist. The three time Grammy considered songwriter, finished several official studio releases and hundreds of tour dates in 2024 showcasing his humble and energetic passion promoting the expansion his story as a Cajun artist. From Mid March to the end of April 2025 Gaspard joined forces with fellow singer songwriter/ banjo savant and partner, Tanner Bingaman of Pennsylvania and set out on a 10k mile tour throughout north western US and Canada. Their journey led to three sold out shows, performing in listening rooms, events centers, libraries and house concerts for hundreds of people. All performances revealed his history in Cajun culture and Acadian roots, highlighting tunes from Gaspard's recent EP Avec le Courant- the story of his ancestral grandmother who traveled as an exiled widow to Louisiana. Gaspard showcased new songs, displaying his "expansion of Cajun music" focused on bilingual
Blues/ Roots/ Americana tunes influenced by Louisiana's forgotten indigenous genre Swamppop
Fall of 2025 Gaspard became the first ever self represented Cajun contestant to air on NBC's The Voice, a nationally televised singing competition where aspiring singers compete for a chance to launch their careers in the music industry. He played harmonica and sang in Cajun French becoming Louisiana’s first contestant to receive a four chair turn. Keeping his performances earnest, genuine, and focused on the story he looks forward to continuing a career representing his home with his art.

12164556757.name: Natu Camara
12164556757.bio:
Natu Camara is a globally celebrated Guinean artist known for her vibrant fusion of Afro-rock, soul, and pop. With a powerful voice and an inspiring message, she has been captivating audiences worldwide while using her platform to uplift and empower.
 
As she continues to tour internationally, Natu remains deeply committed to her humanitarian work through the Dimedi Foundation, which supports education and mentorship for young girls in Guinea.
 
Her latest single, praised by BBC UK Radio, showcases her signature blend of storytelling and rhythm, setting the stage for the launch of another highly anticipated single, followed by her upcoming album. Through her music and activism, Natu Camara spreads light, hope, and positivity across the world, reinforcing her role as a true cultural ambassador and change-maker. 

Read more... https://www.natucamara.com/biography-1

12164539255.name: NOVALIMA
12164539255.bio:
Novalima is one of the most influential and pioneering bands to emerge from Latin America’s global music scene. Blending traditional Afro-Peruvian rhythms and chants with electronic textures, dub, funk, and soul, the Lima-based collective has built a sound that bridges past and future — honoring their roots while pushing boundaries.

Since their debut in 2001, Novalima has been celebrated for redefining Peru’s musical identity and bringing Afro-Peruvian culture to international stages. Their acclaimed album Afro (2005) became a milestone in Latin fusion, followed by Coba Coba, Karimba, Planetario, Ch'usay and La Danza, each expanding their sonic universe and collaborations.

Novalima’s live performances are powerful, hypnotic, and deeply rhythmic experiences — where ancestral percussion meets modern beats in a timeless groove. The band has performed at major festivals around the world, from WOMAD to Roskilde and Central Park SummerStage, earning a devoted global following.

In early 2026, Novalima will release La Danza Remixed, a new album featuring reinterpretations of tracks from their latest record by top producers and DJs from around the world. The band will support the release with a U.S. and Canada tour in April 2026, followed by a European summer tour.

Two decades after their groundbreaking debut, Novalima continues to celebrate cultural fusion, community, and the heartbeat of Afro-Peruvian music — always evolving, always dancing.

12164581350.name: Brewmasters' Talk: Gnarly Barley Brewing Co.
12164581350.bio: Gnarly Barley Brewing Co. originated from the home of Zac and Cari Caramonta. What started in a cramped garage, surrounded by two fat cats and a halfpipe, quickly grew into a passion for crafting exceptional beers. Zac began homebrewing as an exploration into the brewing process after experiencing exceptional craft beers. His mission was to create beers just as excellent as those that inspired him. The Korova Milk Porter and the Hoppopotamus IPA debuted at the 2011 New Orleans on Tap Beer Festival. Encouraged by positive feedback and connections made at local festivals, Zac and Cari opened a 14,000 square foot brewery in Hammond, Louisiana in 2014.

12164581408.name: Boma Bango
12164581408.bio:
Boma Bango takes the hypnotic, reverb drenched, tremolo-ed electric guitar heavy music from the 1960s in the Congo and reimagines it as if it came out of some humid outdoor bar in Southwest Louisiana. Boma Bango formed after Daniel Coolik became infatuated with 1950s and 1960s Congolese Rumba. A music originally influenced by Cuban records from the 1930s and 40s and  infused with melodies and instruments from the Congo.

Boma Bango, by taking musical cues from Congolese luminaries as Franco Luambo Makiadi & le TPOK Jazz, L'Orchestra African Fiesta with Docteur Nico and Tabu Ley Rochereau, and Le Grand Kallé et l'African Jazz, has strived to create their own kind of improvisational music based upon the sounds from this golden age. The band was started in 2018 and currently consists of a collective of musicians from Lafayette and New Orleans.  The band is Daniel Coolik (electric guitar), Trey Boudreaux (bass), Megan Brown Constantin (vocals/percussion), Doug Garrison (drums), Cesar Bacaro (congas/percussion), Tim McFatter (saxophones) and is often augmented with Jafet Perez (drums/percussion), Aurora Nealand (saxophones), or Brad Webb (drums). They reinvent old songs and write new ones in Louisiana French just as the Congolese wrote new songs in Lingala that were inspired by Cuban sounds.  In the same way jazz musicians took the Great American Songbook in the 1940s and 50s and now take from popular music, Boma Bango has reworked these beautiful and almost forgotten melodies to create an alluring, tropical, and exciting new sound.

12164556830.name: GIVERS: "In Light" Live!
12164556830.bio:
In 2010, GIVERS introduced Louisiana and the rest of the world to a fearlessly unique blend of modern and traditional pop, rock, and global influences. The band’s sound formed a crystalline fusion that felt like nostalgia for the future, equal parts joyous immediacy and timeless reflection. This spring, Taylor Guarisco, Tiffany Lamson, Josh Leblanc, Kirby Campbell, and Nick Stephan return as the original lineup to celebrate the 15th anniversary of their debut album, In Light. 
Together, they revisit the awe-inspiring latticework of rich, dense, and powerful songs that defined the record and helped establish GIVERS as a singular creative force. With one foot grounded in technical polyrhythm and the other floating through an ethereal swampland, GIVERS once again invites audiences to follow the light back to the dance floor. It’s a return to the music’s radiant core–offering a guaranteed lift to the spirits, and a reminder of joy, connection, and movement at a moment when it seems we all need it most.

12164553301.name: Brewmasters' Talk: Rally Cap
12164553301.bio:
Just when things might be looking down for the home team, it’s time to throw on the Rally Cap! A superstition? Well maybe…but more than that, it’s a sign of unity and teamwork, a symbol that everyone is working together towards the same goal. Whether you’re playing or you’re just a fan, there is always a strong desire to be part of something bigger. Rally Cap Brewing Company was born out of this desire to create its own “something bigger” – a community of local craft beer drinkers and fans…

Established in 2017, Rally Cap opened its doors to the public on December 14, 2019.

12164533656.name: Yvette Landry Trio
12164533656.bio:
YVETTE LANDRY grew up in Breaux Bridge, Louisiana, not far from the levees of the Atchafalaya Basin, North America’s largest swampland. It was in and around that swamp where she learned an appreciation for the music, dance, stories and language of her Cajun culture. After earning a master’s degree in education and developing a successful teaching career, she began telling stories through song. Playing a variety of instruments in several Cajun bands, Landry also fronts her own band, The Yvette Landry Band. Her debut award-winning album titled “Should Have Known” was released in 2010. (The album was named Offbeat Magazine’s “Best Country/Folk Album” and Landry “Best Country/Folk Artist”).

Over the past several years, Landry has traveled the world and played countless cultural festivals and venues – from the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival to the Bluebird Café in Nashville. She toured Russia and served as a Cultural Ambassador on behalf of the Library of Congress, performing at the Festival of Traditional American Music and gracing the stage at both the Library of Congress and the John F. Kennedy Center of Performing Arts in Washington, DC. 

Yvette Landry is a musician/singer/songwriter who continues to tour worldwide as a multi-instrumentalist, gracing the stage with greats such as Vince Gill & The Time Jumpers, Darrell Scott, Rhonda Vincent, and many more.

State of Louisiana 2013 and 2019 Music Ambassador, Governor to the Memphis Chapter of the Recording Academy, former Director of Louisiana Folk Roots Summer Cajun & Creole Music Kids Camp, and recently inducted into the Louisiana Music Hall of Fame, Landry strives to bring cultures and traditions together, ensuring that they will be passed along.

12164564013.name: Thomé Young
12164564013.bio: It had been a long time since we had heard from Thomé Young—a good seven or eight years. Thomé Young is the alias of Pascal Lejeune, from Pointe-Verte, New Brunswick, who proudly renames himself when he picks up his guitar and turns his poetic observations into songs. It had been a while, because Lejeune is a man of many projects: musician, cultural bistro owner, album producer, assistant director of the Tracadie cultural society, soundtrack composer, carpenter, actor (despite himself). As a result, after the release of his albums Victoria (2014) and Patsy (2017), his guitar sat in its case for five years while he built a house or worked in construction. Now he's back with his family stories and regional tales, delivered with kindness and a sensitivity to his surroundings, to present Dans la vallée, a third record created in the company of Mico Roy (Les Hôtesses d'Hilaire) and Katrine Noël (Les Hay Babies). Thomé Young has performed nearly 500 shows across Canada, France, Belgium, and Slovenia. After a well-deserved break, he is now eager to hit the road again as the next chapter of his career takes shape.

12164519927.name: Sinkane
12164519927.bio:
Ahmed Gallab of Sinkane has always paved his own way, defying all odds and surpassing expectations. With seven albums under his belt and an illustrious career as a composer, producer, and band leader, he has orchestrated remarkable projects. From the resounding revival of William Onyeabor, where a band played without the original main members (take that, Abba!), to writing a musical for the Roald Dahl Foundation, to musical directing Yo-Yo Ma and Angélique Kidjo's "Sarabande Africaine" tour, Gallab’s journey has been extraordinary. Born to Sudanese parents and raised as a hardcore skate punk kid in Ohio.

Sinkane fuses elements of krautrock, prog rock, electronica, reggae, free jazz and funk rock with Sudanese pop to create music inspired by his unique experiences. Despite–or, rather, because of–his unclassifiable sound, The City Slang signee is championed by a multitude of musical legends. Prior to embarking on his solo career, he worked with Eleanor Friedberger, Caribou, of Montreal, Born Ruffians, and Yeasayer as a session musician. As Band Leader and Music Director of the Atomic Bomb! Band, he’s collaborated with rotating group members including  David Byrne (of Talking Heads), Money Mark (of the Beastie Boys), Damon Albarn (of Blur and Gorillaz), Dev Hynes (aka Blood Orange and Lightspeed Champion), Alexis Taylor (of Hot Chip), Charles Lloyd, Amadou and Mariam, Jamie Lidell, Pharoah Sanders, Joshua Redman, among many many others.

12164533657.name: The Babineaux Sisters
12164533657.bio:
The Babineaux Sisters Band has been a dominating force in the music industry for over
a decade, bringing their Cajun sound to audiences far and wide. At the helm of the band are the dynamic sisters, Gracie and Julie Babineaux. Gracie commands the stage as the lead vocalist, accordionist, and fiddler, while Julie holds down the rhythm on bass and contributes back-up vocals. Together, the Babineaux Sisters Band has left their mark on
stages across Louisiana, Florida, Texas, and even as far as Canada. 

Their performances have graced renowned festivals such as Congres de Mondial 2024, Carrefour Mondial De L'Accordion, Festival International, French Quarter Festival, Red River Arts Festival, Mudbug Festival, Festival Acadiens et Creoles, Pensacola's Crawfish Festival, and Festival du Voyageur in Winnipeg,
Manitoba. With four successful albums to their name, a Nashville chart-topping album
with“He’s One of Those”and their latest release "Sans Souliers", the Babineaux Sisters Band continues to assert their position as trailblazers in the world of Cajun music.

12164560996.name: Corey Ledet Zydeco & Black Magic
12164560996.bio:
Two-time GRAMMY®-nominated Zydeco innovator
• Blends various styles of music along with modern
 Zydeco with rich Louisiana tradition
• High-energy performer with global touring 
experience
• Performed in 19 countries and across North America
• 16 albums with GRAMMY® nominations in 2012 and
 2021
• Backed by powerhouse band Black Magic
    • Delivers unforgettable, high-energy live show

12164581208.name: School of Rock Lafayette
12164581208.bio: The School of Rock Lafayette House Band music program gives students under 18 the opportunity to join a gigging band composed of fellow musicians from their school. These students perform additional live shows throughout the year. All students in the Performance Program have the opportunity to audition for a spot in School of Rock Lafayette's House Band. Once selected, House Band members become leaders in their School of Rock community and perform live shows at LA rock venues throughout the year.

12164539396.name: Slap Dragon
12164539396.bio:
Slap Dragon is the brain-child of bassist Scott Mulvahill and vocalist Laura Berens who met and began writing songs together in the summer of 2023. Soul vocals and acoustic instruments (played by some of Nashville's heaviest session musicians) combine for a fresh, funky irresistibly joyful sound that is equal parts bluegrass, disco, and RnB. Slap Dragon played
their first show on June 1st, 2024 to an enthusiastic crowd in Nashville, followed by a set at Bonnaroo. Slap Dragon has begun gaining traction online—including a recent Instagram clip of “Already Won” surpassing 260k views. Following their successful Kickstarter campaign in October 2025, Slap Dragon is set to release their anticipated debut album, "Mission Statement," in 2026.

12164556758.name: The Amazing Nuns
12164556758.bio:
The Amazing Nuns are a rock and roll band from Lafayette, LA. With eight albums and hundreds of live performances, they recently released their first vinyl album titled, Time Wounds All Heels.
They are influenced by 50's Doo Wop, 60's Psychedelic and 70's Punk.

12164533548.name: KC Jones
12164533548.bio: K.C. Jones moves so effortlessly between genres, traditions, and musical concepts that it’s clear she was born with an insatiable artistic curiosity. As a teenager, she emerged from a deeply musical Appalachian family to become an amazingly apt singer, guitarist, and dancer in old-time music. Moving to Southwest Louisiana, she quickly learned Cajun French and began writing preternaturally gifted original songs in dual languages with progressive Cajun bands like GRAMMY-nominated Feufollet, T’Monde, The Daiquiri Queens, and as a duo with Joel Savoy. Both of these jumping off points, what she casually refers to as “obsessions,” have fueled the music on her debut solo record, Queen of the In Between, recently released on June 18, 2021, but she also seamlessly references so much more, everything from classic country to psychedelic rock to contemporary indie roots singer-songwriters. Jones is a fearless bandleader, weaving together an opus that sounds remarkably cohesive. She’s roaming the halls of 20th century Americana synthesizing a century’s worth of music with ease. It’s not simply a meld of seemingly disparate influences; every one of her projects dazzle in their ability to speak to the universality of human emotion.

12164564078.name: Cashier
12164564078.bio: On their debut EP ‘The Weight,’ the Lafayette, Louisiana, four-piece reaches full definition, distilling themes of desire, insecurity, and disconnection into five tightly wound, melody-driven songs released by Julia’s War Recordings, the legendary Philly label founded by Doug Dulgarian of TAGABOW. Across the EP, bandleader Kylie Gaspard’s deeply direct vocal delivery cuts through dense riffs, grounding their songs with her gritty, emotional lyrics. Having recently shared stages with genre titans like Dinosaur Jr., Whirr, Nothing, and Narrow Head, Cashier are building a reputation for a massive sound that resonates far beyond their bayou home.

12164539211.name: Mathieu Lippé
12164539211.bio: Mathieu Lippé is a multidisciplinary artist who blends song, slam poetry, and rap with an inspiring, humanistic voice. A singer, poet, and storyteller, he has toured internationally, won the Granby International Song Festival, and earned a gold medal at the Francophonie Games in Beirut. He has shared the stage with artists such as Francis Cabrel, Loco Locass, and Lynda Lemay, and has written songs for Fred Pellerin, Ima, Brigitte Boisjoli, Amylie, and many others. After nearly 25 years of career and a creative pause, he returns with new song-slam works, including La vie Rêvée and Prélude à la Splendeur (2025).

12164533550.name: F.I.R.E. Expressions Performing Arts Conservatory
12164533550.bio:
F.E. Conservatory is Youth Development x Arts education program providing professional level training in classical and contemporary styles of dance rooted in ethnic and cultural experiences. 

Our mission is to classically train young people while allowing them to develop as an individual, expand their creativity, learn the artistry of dance, and gain insight to the history of traditional dances. We provide arts education, youth development, and a community involvement program that allows not only our students to be inspired and educated through the arts, but people in our community as well.

12164564130.name: Primera Linea
12164564130.bio: Primera Linea is a youth band from Havana, Cuba that fuses AfroCuban rhythms and New Orleans funk. Mentored by AfroCuban funk sensation Cimafunk and New Orleans superstar Trombone Shorty, Primera Linea has developed a dynamic live show and performed at many of Havana’s top venues, including the Fabrica de Arte Cubano (FAC), Tribe Caribe’s Black Box, La Guarida Rooftop, Guampara Music, Bar H and La Carpinteria. The name Primera Linea means “First Line,” as they were the “first” group of youth from their neighborhood to travel to New Orleans to experience and learn Second “Line” music and traditions, which is now a pillar of their music and identity. Antuan (bass), Camila (lead vocals), Daniela (trombone), Fabio (trumpet), Kevin (percussion) and Marlon (keys) are students at the Guillermo Tomas School of Music in Guanabacoa and range in ages from 12 to 18 years old. Primera Linea’s debut album will be released later this year.

12164581238.name: Mike Dean Band
12164581238.bio: Mike Dean and his band have been regulars in the Acadiana music scene for over 20 years. Dege Lege once described the group as “George Jones and Crazy Horse”.  In recent years the band has ventured beyond the comfort of their South Louisiana community, playing weeklong residencies in Key West, providing afternoon entertainment to roots music fans at the venerable Gruene Hall, and in support of their old friend Drew Landry at venues and festivals across Montana.  Their latest single (God Loves Ya When Ya Dance) is available on all streaming platforms.

12164519929.name: Acadiana Symphony Youth Orchestra
12164519929.bio:
ASYO is a dynamic ensemble of talented young string musicians from Lafayette and surrounding areas of Acadiana, bringing together students from diverse schools and backgrounds who share a passion for musical excellence. The orchestra provides advanced performance opportunities for dedicated young artists, emphasizing strong ensemble skills, expressive playing, and musical curiosity.
Through rehearsals, concerts, and outreach performances, the ensemble explores a wide range of repertoire—from classical masterworks to contemporary and culturally inspired music—encouraging students to grow as confident, versatile musicians. In addition to technical development, members gain valuable experience in collaboration, discipline, and artistic leadership.
ASYO  is proud to perform at the Festival International de Louisiane, celebrating the power of music to connect cultures, generations, and communities through shared artistic expression.

12164533715.name: The Revelers
12164533715.bio: The Revelers have been bringing their party around the world for nearly 10 years. With their long-awaited follow-up to 2016’s Grammy-nominated record, the band has taken their place firmly at the top of a game where they make the rules.  The brash blasts of the accordion, the shuffle of feet, the wailing vocals in old French… The sound of Cajun music is well-known throughout the United States and abroad. But for Louisiana-based band The Revelers, it’s just the start of the story. Headquartered in the city of Lafayette in Southwest Louisiana’s Cajun Country (New Orleans is home to jazz, but not a native home to Cajun music), the band is dedicated to the “holy trinity” of Cajun culture: hot music, all-night dancing, and great food. But they’re determined to explore the larger world of Louisiana music as well, and with their new album, The End of the River (Au bout de la rivière), they’re tapping into their deep lifetimes of knowledge of Swamp Pop, Zydeco, and old-school Louisiana dancehall music. They’ve synthesized all of these different traditions into a new sound, their own sound.

12164518541.name: Subatomic Sound System + Screechy Dan + Norwood Fisher
12164518541.bio: NYC’s Subatomic Sound System has been on a 2 decade mission forging a future foundation style built on the bass heavy, spacious soundscapes, and live improvisational remixing of classic 1970s Jamaican dub and conscious reggae music in the context of electronic bass music. For the 2nd decade, Subatomic Sound System was the Brooklyn based touring band for Jamaican dub & reggae inventor Lee "Scratch" Perry (1936-2021) and producers of the acclaimed 2017 album "Super Ape Returns to Conquer" which reimagined Scratch's 1973 classic "Super Ape", mixing the vintage Jamaican dub sound with 21st century bass and beats.  Using the latest technology, they pioneered a unique performance style that blurs the lines between DJing and a live band. These efforts gained the attention of dub and reggae pioneer Lee "Scratch" Perry, the genius producer and song writer behind Bob Marley, who subsequently employed Subatomic Sound as his go to band for re-inventing his Black Ark Studio sound live on stage.  Subatomic is spearheaded by producer, DJ, and multi-instrumentalist Emch, who arranges and manipulates both prerecorded music instruments and effects with the live musicians to create a real time musical dialogue. The core live musicians include Jamaican hall of fame percussionist and Black Ark veteran Larry McDonald (Skatalites, Gil Scot Heron, Peter Tosh), Troy Shaka Simms (Brooklyn Gypsies, Mobius Collective) on sax and horn arrangements, and on the microphone, the legendary Brooklyn via Jamaica singjay Screechy Dan chatting & singing every which way.  Renowned special guest Norwood Fisher of Fishbone joins on the bass.  Subatomic has toured as live band, sound system, or selector across the USA, Canada, UK, Europe, Middle East, Russia, India, and Mexico including appearances at France's Telerama Dub Festival, The Marley’s Kayafest, Coachella, Hungary’s Ozora Festival, SoleDXB, Cali Roots, Cali Vibes, Hollywood Bowl and openin...

12164533663.name: Lafayette Lion Dance
12164533663.bio: We are a local traditional Vietnamese Lion Dance troupe! Lion dance is a form of performance art that is found all over Asia that involves the manipulation of a life-sized lion puppet to the beat of a traditional drum and cymbals. It is normally performed to bring about good luck to events such as during Lunar New Year, a marriage ceremony, or the opening of a new business. Come and see us perform!

12164560865.name: Steve Riley & the Mamou Playboys
12164560865.bio:
Steve Riley and the Mamou Playboys began thirty-five years ago with a reputation for excellence. Their stunningly clean and cohesive performance of Cajun French music from the backwaters of Southwest Louisiana propelled them into the world music limelight early on, and by their third release, Trace of Time, had garnered them a Grammy nomination in the worldwide field of traditional folk music, another in 2004 for Bon Reve, in 2009 for Live at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival and again in 2011 for their release, Grand Isle.

From the day they started, they have gone from strength to strength. Never before in Cajun music has a comparable wealth of skills been brought to the same table.

When all that heart and all that skill focus on the revelry of a hot two-step, then turn on a dime and deliver an a cappella ballad, then play something that sounds like Howlin’ Wolf fell in love with a Creole girl, you’ve found the most Cajun music you can find in any one spot. You’ve found Steve Riley and the Mamou Playboys.

12164553342.name: Dwight James & the Royals
12164553342.bio:
Dwight James, lead vocalist and guitarist of Dwight James & the Royals, channels the spirit of classic soul, blues, and R&B with a sound that is as timeless as it is fresh. Drawing inspiration from the iconic sounds of the 60s and 70s, James blends heartfelt storytelling with smooth vocals and rich melodies, inviting listeners to experience a blend of both past and present in every performance.

With a dedication to music that resonates across generations, Dwight James & the Royals continue to build a loyal fanbase, bringing an unforgettable blend of nostalgia and innovation to the modern music scene. Need Your Loving, James' debut EP, received notable acclaim, earning airplay on BBC Radio 6 and a spot on Bandcamp.com’s “Best Soul Albums of 2018.” Currently signed with the Brooklyn-based licensing agency Low Profile, James and the Royals are poised to make an even greater impact with their signature sound.

12164518563.name: Beauséjour
12164518563.bio: Beauséjour has extensively toured Canada celebrating their French Culture. The duo brings Acadia and the Prairies together through the award winning voices of Joannie Benoit and Jocelyne Baribeau. Their warm and captivating music blends accents, styles, and stories.

12164556832.name: Blue Monday Allstars Celebrate Lee Allen Zeno
12164556832.bio: At Blue Monday, we're more than a concert series; we're a community movement powered by volunteers, sponsors, and donors. It's their unwavering dedication that helps us bring the best to every corner of our community. Our extended musical family, including renowned guest artists, blesses us with unforgettable performances. Impromptu appearances and collaborations transform every quarter into an extraordinary night.

12164581358.name: Sally Baby's Silver Dollars
12164581358.genre: Neo-classic New Orleans R&B dance hall music and Creole/Gypsy Jazz.
12164581358.bio:
Sally Baby’s Silver Dollars are breaking out in New Orleans and nationwide with their fresh take on retro New Orleans R&B dance hall music and Creole Jazz.   

They were 2nd runners up in NPR’s prestigious 2024 Tiny Desk competition and their exciting sound has taken the group from playing tiny dives in New Orleans' 9th Ward to profile bookings at the Jazz & Heritage Festival and French Quarter Festival at home, and coveted festivals nationwide like California's High Sierra Music Festival and Upstate NY's Finger Lakes GrassRoots Festival.

Founded by Singer-guitarist, composer, music historian, and New Orleans jazz tour guide Salvatore Geloso (Sally Baby), the ensemble has recently released their debut self-titled EP to glowing reviews.   Geloso’s songs are at the center of Sally Baby’s Silver Dollars' music with Salvatore's original compositions - taking center stage.

All of the ensemble's musicians have extensive resumes - some with classical training and serious chops - including Geloso, who has studied not only New Orleans' music, but also opera and choral works like Mozart’s “Requiem.”

When you listen to this band, Sal's compositions shine, but Geloso brings so much more than just his songs to the group's live experience. With his background in theater and with working recent years guiding jazz music tours through the French Quarter, Sally Baby's mission is to immerse every listener into New Orleans rich music and cultural history.

Like the many unique New Orleans bands preceding them, the Silver Dollars  leap into a greater National consciousness is - no doubt - on the eminent horizon.

12164533790.name: Bas Clas
12164533790.bio:
Bas Clas (a slang Cajun phrase meaning "low class") brings a fiercely original blend of rock energy and South Louisiana storytelling that has been evolving for nearly 5 decades.

The band was formed in the wet winter of 1976 by brothers Donnie and Steve Picou, with bassist Geoff Thistlethwaite joining in 1978. Known for marathon live shows and a relentless commitment to original music, Bas Clas gained a loyal following through weekly performances in Lafayette that helped catalyze the city’s original-music scene.

In the early 1980s, their music caught the attention of legendary producer John Hammond (Billie Holiday, Bob Dylan, Bruce Springsteen, Stevie Ray Vaughan), who championed the band’s songwriting and distinctive sound.

Deeply rooted in Acadiana's musical culture, Bas Clas blends rock energy with the storytelling traditions of South Louisiana. In recent years, the band has returned to the studio for a series of recordings at Dockside Studio, releasing multiple albums while continuing to evolve their sound.

12164539378.name: Zachary Richard
12164539378.bio: Zachary Richard, born 1950, Scott, Louisiana.  Cultural activist,  environmentalist, poet, singer and songwriter.  Graduated Tulane University (cum laude), 1972.  Chevalier de l’Ordre de la Pléiade.  Membre de l’Ordre des Francophones d’Amérique, Member Order of Canada. Officier de l’Ordre des Palmes Académiques et Commandeur de l’Ordre des Arts et Lettres de la République Française.  First French language poet laureat of Louisiana. Prix Leger-Comeau (Société Nationale des Acadiens) Prix Marquis de Lafayette (Fondation Louisiane). Doctor Honoris Causa :  University of Moncton (Nouveau Brunswick), University of Ottawa, University Sainte Anne (Nova Scotia) & the University of  Louisiana at Lafayette.  Best known for his musical career spanning 50 years and including over 20 albums in a style uniquely his own.

12164556847.name: Vieux Farka Touré
12164556847.bio:
Often referred to as “The Hendrix of the Sahara”, Vieux Farka Touré was born in Niafunké, Mali in 1981. He is the son of legendary Malian guitar player Ali Farka Touré, who died in 2006. Ali Farka Touré came from a historical tribe of soldiers, and defied his parents in becoming a musician. When Vieux was in his teens, he declared that he also wanted to be a musician. His father disapproved due to the pressures he had experienced being a musician. Rather, he wanted Vieux to become a soldier. But with help from family friend the kora maestro Toumani Diabaté, Vieux eventually convinced his father to give him his blessing to become a musician shortly before Ali passed.

Vieux was initially a drummer / calabash player at Mali’s Institut National des Arts, but secretly began playing guitar in 2001. Ali Farka Touré was weakened with cancer when Vieux announced that he was going to record an album. Ali recorded a couple of tracks with him, and these recordings, which can be heard on Vieux’s debut CD, were amongst his final ones.

Born out of the studio Vieux built at his family's compound (which he named 'Studio Ali Farka Toure' in honor of his late father) came the album 'Les Racines' (released June 2022), which sees Vieux masterfully return to the deep roots of the Desert Blues music that his father introduced to the world and Vieux spent most of his career to date exploring, experimenting with, and expanding. 2022 also saw the release of a long-awaited collaborative album between Vieux and Houston-based psych-rock superstars Khruangbin called ‘Ali’ - an album on which the artists join forces to pay homage to Ali Farka Toure by reimagining eight of his songs together.  With each new project Vieux broadens his horizons, embraces new challenges and further entrenches his reputation as one of the world’s most talented and innovative musicians.

12164533746.name: Delgres
12164533746.bio: Drums that are both metronomic and feline, a dobro-guitar with riffs made from embers, telluric basslines that seem to escape from a dented tuba… Here is Delgres, a power-trio that’s reinventing the blues by injecting an abrasive rock transe in it, recalling the Tuaregs’ soul as much as The Black Keys or John Lee Hooker’s, while carrying Louis Delgres’ secular message : his heroic fight against slavery in the Guadeloupe island. This is how this rebellious and burning music means so much nowadays, by speaking to us through shivers, and vibrating our bodies as well as our minds.

12164553331.name: Geno Delafose & French Rockin' Boogie
12164553331.bio:
Geno Delafose (born February 6, 1971 in Eunice, Louisiana) is a zydeco accordionist and singer. His sound is deeply rooted in traditional Creole music with strong influences from Cajun music and also country and western. His father is the famous zydeco accordion player John Delafose.
Delafose was born and raised in Eunice, Louisiana. At the age of eight, he joined his father’s band, the Eunice Playboys as a rubboard player and continued to play with the band until his father’s death in 1994. He also appeared on the several of the bands recordings. He switched to the accordion in the early 1990s and started to play as an opening act for his father.
In 1994, he debuted with album French Rockin’ Boogie on Rounder Records. The name of this album also became the name of his band with whom he still plays with today. He released two more albums from the label, before signing with Time Square label to release Everybody’s Dancin’ in 2003. He has also appeared on the compilation album Creole Bred: A Tribute to Creole & Zydeco released in 2004 on Vanguard Records

12164518543.name: Burke Riley Trio
12164518543.bio:
Burke Riley, 16 year old son of legendary Cajun musician Steve Riley, began his musical journey at a very early age. By age 3, Burke was already onstage sitting in with the band Courtbouillon and the Mamou Playboys playing drums, his groove solid and natural talent undeniable even at such an early age. By age 5 he transferred his rhythm skills to acoustic guitar, a natural progression that lead to his deepening knowledge of the importance of Cajun music’s groove. 

He picked up accordion at age 6,  excelling quickly, tackling some of Cajun music’s most complex melodies. This kind hearted, talented young man, will wow you with is incredible musical ability and command of whatever instrument he plays! He’s one of the new generation, quickly taking his place among the greats with whom he was raised playing!

12164560877.name: Las Cafeteras
12164560877.bio:
Las Cafeteras have taken the music scene by storm with their infectious live performances and have crossed many genres and borders along the way. Their electric sound & energy has taken them around the world playing shows from Bonnaroo to the Hollywood Bowl, WOMAD New Zealand to Montreal Jazz, & beyond!

Born and raised East of the Los Angeles River, Las Cafeteras are remixing roots music as modern day troubadours.  They are a sonic explosion of Afro-Mexican rhythms, electronic beats and powerful rhymes that document stories of a community seeking to ‘build a world where many world fit.’

From Afro-Mexican to Americana, from Soul to Son Jarocho, from Roots to Rock and Hip Hop, Las Cafeteras take folk music to the future.

12164581330.name: Voices of Progressive Gospel Choir
12164581330.bio:
Voices of Progressive, better known as "VOP", was founded in 1967 at the Progressive Baptist Church, Lafayette, LA, which is currently under the leadership of Pastor Lloyd Joiner, Jr.  VOP was birthed out of a vision by its first director, Ada Ruth Thomas.  From the onset, VOP invoked congregants and followers to get personally involved in corporate worship.  VOP's ministry goal and purpose is to lift up God's Kingdom as His Lyrical Ambassadors.  VOP has been afforded well-versed Choir Directors such as Clark Joseph, (the late) Lerone Rubin, (the late) Darryl Jefferson, Mechelle Jefferson, and currently, Melete W. Terry.
VOP's exquisite harmonies and stirring gospel repertoire compelled them to record several albums, headline numerous concerts with gospel and secular artists, and exercise active involvement in events around the Tri-State Region.  The spirit and energy VOP continues to emanate comes from a desire to let others know that the loving God we sing about is real, their faith has been increased, and their hope has been renewed.

12164519996.name: Michael Juan Nunez
12164519996.bio: Michael Juan Nunez is a singer, guitarist, songwriter, from South Louisiana whose music taps into the heart of American southern culture. It’s fresh, and urgent, yet unmistakably sprouting from very deep roots. His music paints pictures of life, as seen through the eyes of southern Louisiana. His guitar playing is raw and passionate…moaning, screaming, singing, and driving modern day melodies, with echoes of long lost dancehalls.

12164564098.name: Stephen Marley
12164564098.bio:
Stephen Marley is an eight-time GRAMMY Award–winning recording artist, singer, songwriter, musician, and producer. His career includes collaborations with artists such as Lauryn Hill, Pitbull, Shaggy, Nas, and Erykah Badu, as well as extensive work alongside his family.

His most recent album, Old Soul, was released in September 2023 via Tuff Gong Collective/UMe/Ghetto Youths International. The acoustic-based project spans multiple genres and cultural influences and features guest appearances from Bob Weir, Eric Clapton, Jack Johnson, Ziggy Marley, Damian “Jr. Gong” Marley, Buju Banton, and Slightly Stoopid.

In addition to his prolific recording work, Stephen served as musical director for the feature film Bob Marley: One Love (2024). The film received multiple NAACP Image Award nominations, and its soundtrack, Bob Marley: One Love – Music Inspired by the Film (Deluxe), won the GRAMMY Award for Best Reggae Album in 2025.

Stephen Marley continues to tour extensively throughout the US and beyond.  Recent highlights include a special Bob Marley 80th Birthday performance on Stick Figure’s U.S. Summer Tour, headlining dates and the 25+ date Traffic Jam North American Tour with Damian Marley—including performances at Red Rocks Amphitheatre and the Hollywood Bowl—and The Marley Brothers’ Legacy Tour, marking the first national U.S. shed tour by the brothers in over two decades. 

Stephen is currently in the studio working on multiple projects slated for release in 2026. For music, tour dates, and additional information, visit www.stephenmarleymusic.com.

12164581335.name: Prends Courage
12164581335.bio:
In the heart of Lafayette, where Cajun spirit meets creative fervor, Prends Courage was born. This dynamic band is a testament to the power of music to transcend time and circumstance, inspired by the passing of Christopher Stafford and the enduring legacy of Feufollet’s “Prends Courage”.

With a sonic tapestry woven from the threads of tradition and innovation, Prends Courage conjures the essence of Cajun music's past, present, and future. Jamie Lynn Fontenot’s guitar and vocals, Luke Huval’s accordion and angelic vocals, Elise Riley’s drums, Jo Vidrine's bass, and Kelli Jones’s fiddle and vocals blend in a joyful celebration of life, love, and resilience.

As they take the stage, Prends Courage embodies the joie de vivre that defines their heritage, inviting all to join in the dance, the song, and enthusiasm that flows from their very being. Prends Courage shines bright, a beacon of light and laughter, reminding us all to prends courage – take heart – and let the music set us free.

12164539402.name: $ideQue$t ft. Gino V. and Zach Edwards
12164539402.bio: Hailing from Lafayette, Louisiana, $ideQue$t(Side Quest) is a soul-drenched blues rock project steeped in Southern heat. The joint vision of singer-songwriters Gino V. and Zach Edwards blends gritty guitar and bayou groove with smooth R&B textures into a sound that hits hard and moves easy. What began as a few duo gigs together quickly progressed into cowriting music and eventually booking a handful of full band shows. After a few of these musical moments, V. and Edwards realized this lighting in a bottle might be something they want to explore a little further.  Though they each had their own respective projects, it was incredibly obvious to the pair that they tap into something special when they are on stage together and $ideQue$t was officially formed. The southern based project channels the spirit of the Gulf Coast into a sound that feels lived-in, restless, and alive. $ideQue$t blurs the genre line while keeping the feel front and center—music meant to be felt as much as it’s heard.

12164520006.name: Bonsoir, Catin
12164520006.bio: Bonsoir, Catin is a female-powered Cajun supergroup from Southwest Louisiana. They burst upon the local Acadiana music-scene 2006 and have been rocking the local dancehalls and bringing their brand of authentic yet progressive Cajun music to a wider audience on the national and worldwide stage ever since. Members of Bonsoir, Catin Kristi Guillory (accordion), Anya Burgess (fiddle; Magnolia Sisters), Christine Balfa (guitar, Balfa Toujours), Maegan Berard (electric guitar; Sweet Cecilia), Ashley Hayes (bass guitar), and have an infection onstage chemistry that brings joy and fun to all audiences. With four full-length albums, their third release, Light the Stars (2016) was nominated for a Grammy award in the Regional Roots category.

12164563940.name: Vishten
12164563940.bio:
Rooted in the windswept shores of Prince Edward Island and the Magdalen Islands on Canada’s east coast, Vishtèn brings more than two decades of Acadian musical tradition and innovation to the world stage. Emmanuelle LeBlanc, Pascal Miousse, and Megan Bergeron grew up in close-knit Acadian communities where music was learned through family gatherings, community dances, and intergenerational transmission.

The group began when Emmanuelle and her twin sister Pastelle joined creative forces with Pascal, forming a trio that would become one of Canada’s leading folk ensembles. Megan, who grew up alongside the LeBlanc family and appeared on Vishtèn’s debut album, has recently rejoined the group—bringing continuity, shared language, and renewed artistic momentum.

With over 3,000 performances and more than 60 international tours, Vishtèn has performed across Europe, Australia, New Zealand, the U.K., and the United States. Their dynamic blend of fiddle, piano, foot percussion, step dance, and original compositions has been featured at major festivals including Celtic Connections, the Festival Interceltique de Lorient, New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, Milwaukee Irish Fest, Woodford Folk Festival, and the Vancouver Olympic Games.

In 2024, Vishtèn released Expansion, a powerful project built from the unfinished musical ideas of Pastelle LeBlanc. Celebrated for its emotional depth and collaborative spirit, the album won Album of the Year at both the 2025 East Coast Music Awards and Music PEI Awards, alongside multiple genre awards. With Megan reunited alongside Emmanuelle and Pascal, Vishtèn continues to honour Acadian tradition while forging new creative paths.

12164527131.name: Nathan & the Zydeco Cha Chas
12164527131.genre: 40 year history as SW Louisiana's pioneering Creole zydeco ambassadors.
12164527131.bio:
Nathan & the Zydeco Cha Chas (Lafayette, Louisiana / USA):    

 

Blessed with a 65th Grammy Awards nomination for his recording Lucky Man, Nathan Williams is a zydeco legend that has over three and a half decades under his hat as one of Southwest Louisiana’s most beloved Creole music pioneers and cultural ambassadors.       Whether he is performing at the likes of NYC’s Lincoln Center or Carnegie Hall’s CityWide Concert Series, DC’s Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival, Nashville’s Grand Ole Opry, Europe’s top blues festivals or down home at his brother’s famous El Sido’s Zydeco & Blues Club in Lafayette, Louisiana, Nathan and his top-shelf Nathan & the Zydeco Cha Chas band never fail to get audiences up and shakin’ a leg to their un-rivaled stomp-down zydeco party!

 

     Williams started his professional music career at 21, recording 45rpm singles for his brother’s El Sid-O’s lable.   Sid later opened up his historic El Sid-O’s Zydeco and Blues Club in Lafayette and the Cha Chas soon became the Friday night residence artist for the venue. 

 

     Nathan’s big break came when Buckwheat Zydeco recommended him to Rounder Records.   Nathan auditioned for the label and secured a contract and which led to him founding Nathan & the Zydeco Cha Chas in 1985.   In 1988 Nathan first performed at the New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival – where he has returned each and every year since that date.

 

     It wasn’t long that Williams was noticed by The New York Times who stated that, at age 25, he was “poised to become important” in revitalizing zydeco music.   Nathan’s music blends zydeco, jazz, blues and R&B, with most of his original songs composed by Williams.

 

    For over 35 years, Nathan & the Zydeco Cha Chas have toured extensively – performing everywhere from local Louisiana festival and dance halls to the most important stages throughout the Globe.

 

 

 “If you don’t get up an...

12164581279.name: Beau Cheval
12164581279.bio: Beau Cheval plays French music that evokes the traditional sounds of South Louisiana and Acadia into an all original repertoire.

12164561040.name: Jacques Surette
12164561040.bio:
Jacques Surette is a 25-year-old singer-songwriter from Yarmouth, Nova Scotia, whose natural charm is captivating. He started playing guitar at age 12 and began writing his own songs at 14. He initially writes songs in French and English, but quickly realized that French was the language he wanted to use to express himself through music. He writes lyrics that take listeners on a journey through his corner of the country. He first made a name for himself in the Maritimes, but has also gained recognition in Quebec, Louisiana, Switzerland, and France. He offers intimate performances and school workshops where he emphasizes the importance of creating in French. His show takes listeners on a journey through his corner of the country, SouthEast Nova Scotia, and invites them to discover his local dialect, Acadjonne, and his life as a young artist.
 
In June 2019, he released his first folk-pop album, "Marche, marche, marche", co-produced by Lisa LeBlanc and Benoit Morier. His second album, "Jacques Surette II' (2020), was produced by Mike Trask and Christien Belliveau. It is a bilingual album with folk country influences for the French-language tracks and alternative rock for the English songs. His third album, "Conséquences" (2023), was produced by Éric Dion and André Lavergne (Dans l'Shed). His fourth album, "Les vieux chapeaux" (October 16, 2025), which was recorded with an all-Nova Scotian team, is co-produced by Charles Robicheau and Jacques Surette. All four of his albums are released on the Acadian label Le Grenier musique.

12164518626.name: Breabach
12164518626.bio:
Securely ranked among Scotland’s most skilled and imaginative contemporary folk acts, Breabach unite deep roots in Highland and Island tradition with the innovative musical ferment of their Glasgow base. They have released six increasingly acclaimed albums, whilst fuelling their creative appetites in collaborations with indigenous Australasian artists Moana and the Tribe & The Black Arm Band, Quebec’s Le Vent du Nord, video game composer Big Giant Circles and as artists-in-residence at the 2019 Celtic Colours festival with Cape Bretoners, Beolach. 2020 saw the introduction of the supremely talented, multi-instrumentalist Conal McDonagh to the band which coincided with the production and release of ‘Dùsgadh’, a newly commissioned short film in with original score in collaboration with BAFTA award winning animator Cat Bruce. 

Their 17 year adventure has included live performances from Sydney Opera House to Central Park NY. They have racked up an impressive array of accolades including five Scots Trad Music Awards, nominations as ‘Best Group’ in the BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards and ‘European Album of the Year’ in The Songlines Music Awards. The band are also currently nominated as Best Group  in the BBC Scotland Trad awards due to be decided in December 2022.
 
Breabach are; Megan Henderson (Fiddle, Vocals, Step Dance), James Lindsay (Double Bass, Vocals), Calum MacCrimmon (Bagpipes, Whistle, Bouzouki, Vocals), Conal McDonagh (Bagpipes, Whistle, Vocals) and Ewan Robertson (Guitar, Vocals, Cajon). Acknowledging and respecting the origins of both the music they play and the roots of the band whilst embracing the future with new ideas, energy and belief is a key attribute of the band and has remained  a constant theme throughout their 17 years.

12164556851.name: Chris Ardoin & Zydeco Nu-Step
12164556851.bio: Internationally known for his soulful vocals and music composition, Chris Ardoin is one of the most sought after artists / producers in the industry today. He has traveled and performed in all 50 states as well as overseas in London, Japan, Sweden, Amsterdam, Brazil, Australia, Germany, Jamaica, Mexico, Paris, and Cayman Islands.  Breaking attendance records from Louisiana nightclubs to Carnegie Hall in New York City to Carnivale in South America, Chris is bringing zydeco music, creole culture, & southern soul music to new heights.

12164518843.name: Jourdan Thibodeaux et les Rôdailleurs
12164518843.bio:
Jourdan Thibodeaux is the guy you picture when someone says the word “authentic.” Straight from the blackjack boggy woods of Cypress Island, Louisiana, Jourdan is one of only a small number of young people speaking Cajun French today, and his soulful singing and fiddling are the perfect medium for his ever-growing repertoire of original Louisiana French songs. His musical ability and his crafty songwriting which is at once classic and progressive has afforded him a band comprised of some of the finest artists in Acadiana today. 
   He has been featured on 60 minutes, and programs on Travel Channel, Discovery, TV5, France24, PBS, CBC, CNN with Anthony Bourdain, several documentaries, including the award winning “Roots of Fire”, and more.          
   Whether he is playing music festivals across the US and internationally, or being the Capitaine of the traditional courir de Mardi Gras, catching alligators in the Atchafalaya Basin, or teaching Louisiana French online, Jourdan is always a dedicated ambassador of Cajun and Creole culture.

12164519844.name: Silver Birds Steel Orchestra
12164519844.genre: Reggae, roots, rock, pop, latin, rnb.
12164519844.bio:
Silver Birds Steel Orchestra – A symphony of Jamaican Excellence
In the heart of Jamaica's pulsating cultural scene, the Silver Birds Steel Orchestra emerges as a true musical gem. Established in 2007 by the visionary master drummer and instructor, Dean Barnett, this dynamic ensemble began as a social outreach program for inner-city high school children in Kingston. Over the years, it has evolved into a prominent steel pan ensemble known for its high-energy performances and diverse musical repertoire.
The orchestra gained international recognition after winning five gold medals at the 2009 and 2010 World Performing Arts Olympics in Los Angeles. Their performances span reggae, roots, rock, jazz, Latin, pop, and other genres.
Silver Birds has performed for major events and organizations, including the United States Embassy, British High Commission, Jamaica Jazz and Blues Festival, Jambana Festival (Canada), Shaggy & Friends, and various Royal Caribbean cruise ships. They maintain regular engagements at leading hotels and resorts such as Sandals, SuperClubs, RIU, Hilton, Half Moon, Jewel Resorts, Moon Palace, GoldenEye, Azul Resorts, and Gran Bahia.
The orchestra has also performed for corporate clients including Mitsubishi, Air Canada, Delta, Royal Caribbean, GraceKennedy, and Caribbean Airlines. A seven-member touring group represents the ensemble internationally, promoting Jamaican culture through music and choreography.
Silver Birds was voted Jamaica’s top-performing band in 2009 by the RJR Group and completed consecutive three-month residencies at Ocean Chimelong in China.
Today, the Silver Birds Steel Orchestra are ambassadors of Jamaican culture, bringing the island's charm to the international stage. They continue to perform at private functions, festivals, and global events, representing Jamaica through their musical skill, versatility, and cultural impact.

12164518545.name: Battle of the Bands:  2nd place (DINGER) & 1st place (5AM)
12164518545.bio: LOCAL SONGWRITERS OF ALL AGES AND GENRES

12164539528.name: Rusty Metoyer & the Zydeco Krush
12164539528.bio:
Lake Charles native, Rusty Metoyer, is one of southwest Louisiana’s premier stars. Metoyer and his unique brand of Zydeco music have thrilled audiences from California to New York, in Holland and France, and every weekend from Houston to New Orleans. Rusty Metoyer was immersed in Creole music from a young age. Both of his grandfathers were Creole musicians. However, he didn’t pick up the accordion until the age of 14 after both grandfathers had passed away and he felt that someone needed to keep the tradition going in the family. In 2010, his senior year of high school, he formed the band Rusty Metoyer and The Zydeco Krush.
 
Metoyer and his band perform regularly in Louisiana and Texas and beyond for a wide variety of events, including festivals, night clubs, trail rides, corporate events, casinos, and private parties. What makes Metoyer’s music unique are the noticeable influences from many different genres such as funk, rock and roll, rhythm and blues, country, hip hop, and soul. Rusty Metoyer and the Zydeco Krush have released six albums: King of I-10 (2025), Comin' in Hot Vol. 2: Some Originals, Some Covers, All Bangerz (2024), Comin' in Hot Vol. 1: Live in Lake Charles (2024), Unlike Any Other (2022), In Due Time (2016) and Take My Hand (2013) and three singles: HYPE (2023), Riverbank (2019) and Hurricane Proof (2020). He is also a member of the creole super group known as Creole United, featuring seasoned creole musicians Andre Thierry, Sean Ardoin, Ed Poullard, and Lawrence Ardoin.
